To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) novice consumers are more likely to be influenced by the source of a message than are expert consumers; and (2) novice consumers are also more likely to be persuaded by a message when they are in a state of uncertainty.

1) consumers are not passive recipients of advertising, but are active participants, who interpret and evaluate advertising messages, 2) consumers are not a homogenous group, but are diverse in their knowledge and expertise, 3) the way consumers interpret advertising messages is related to their knowledge and expertise with the product category, and 4) consumers' knowledge and expertise are related to their level of experience with the product category.

(1) novice and expert consumers differ on a number of dimensions; (2) novice and expert consumer behavior is influenced by different cognitive processes; and (3) novice and expert consumption is affected by different environmental factors.
